submissions.title: AG Mayes calls for statewide pause on new data center construction
submissions.excerpt: The only sane thing to do is to pause the approval of new data centers, Mayes said in a statement.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes is asking the legislature and Gov. Katie Hobbs to pass a law pausing approval of new (especially hyperscale) data centers statewide, citing rising electricity bills and a ~30% federal cut to Arizona's Colorado River water allocation. This is a call for future legislation, not an enacted restriction -- no bill exists yet, so no project should be marked as blocked based on this alone. Not linked to a specific tracked project; flagging for the siting-restrictions review.

submissions.title: Perryville revises data center regulations after public concerns
submissions.excerpt: requiring a closed-loop cooling system capped at 50,000 gallons per day
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Perryville, Missouri's Board of Aldermen was set to consider a third revision of the city's data center ordinance on Sept. 1, 2026 (its first version passed Feb. 2026, a second version followed). The draft under consideration adds a 500-foot setback from homes/childcare/developmental-disability work centers, a public-hearing requirement before licensing, a water-use cap generally at 50,000 gallons/day (30-day average), mandatory closed-loop cooling, a groundwater-well and once-through-cooling ban, and required environmental/noise impact assessments. I could not confirm the Sept. 1 vote outcome in available coverage as of this report (today is Sept. 2) -- worth a follow-up look to see whether it was adopted. No live data center project is currently sited/proposed in Perryville per this coverage (city says one company inquired, nothing submitted).

submissions.title: Legislature approves McNerney bill to ensure data centers pay their fair share of energy costs
submissions.excerpt: SB 1168 will ensure large energy users pay their fair share.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION (utility connection rule): California's SB 1168 (Sen. Jerry McNerney) passed the Assembly unanimously and the Senate 38-0 on Sept. 1, 2026, and now heads to Gov. Newsom's desk (not yet signed as of this report). It directs the CPUC to set rate structures ensuring data centers pay their proportionate share of transmission/distribution and load-growth costs rather than spreading them across all ratepayers. Statewide policy, not tied to one project -- flagging for the siting-restrictions review.

submissions.title: Pinal County board rejects massive data center project
submissions.excerpt: Pinal County officials blocked the path forward for Vermaland's La Osa Energy Center on Aug. 26 in a 4-1 vote.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Pinal County (AZ) Board of Supervisors voted 4-1 on Aug. 26, 2026 to reject rezoning for Vermaland's La Osa Energy Center near Eloy -- among the largest data center proposals ever floated in Arizona (11 buildings, a 500MW on-site gas plant, up to 1GW total demand). Rejection stood even after developers offered an 80% scale-back, self-imposed water-use limits, and a commitment to cover all energy infrastructure costs. Cited by Arizona's AG (see companion finding on the statewide pause call) as an example of local pushback. Not a currently tracked project -- flagging as a new, now-blocked proposal rather than proposing a project row, since it was killed at rezoning.
